analysis.evidence: The verse names Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash as the sons of Aram. In this genealogy, אֲרָם names their father.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. It completes the construct phrase וּבְנֵי אֲרָם, “and the sons of Aram.”
analysis.sense: Aram, the father of Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash

evidence.note: עוּץ immediately follows וּבְנֵי אֲרָם, “and the sons of Aram,” as the first of four names.

article.name: עוּץ
article.summary: Genesis lists Uz first among the sons of Aram. The meaning of the name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for עוּץ with the gloss “Uz.” The genealogy gives no support for the source gloss “peel.”
draft.definition: Uz, a son of Aram named in Genesis 10:23.
draft.evidence: The heading וּבְנֵי אֲרָם identifies Uz and the three men listed after him as sons of Aram.

analysis.evidence: וּבְנֵי אֲרָם means “and the sons of Aram.” עוּץ is the first name in that list, followed by Hul, Gether, and Mash. The verse identifies the bearer but gives no derivation for his name.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun, a masculine personal name with no prefix or suffix.

evidence.note: The list of Aram’s sons places Hul between Uz and Gether.

article.name: חוּל
article.summary: Hul is named second among the sons of Aram. The meaning of his name is uncertain.

analysis.evidence: The phrase וּבְנֵי אֲרָם “and the sons of Aram” introduces a list of names. חוּל follows עוּץ and precedes גֶּתֶר. The list identifies Hul by parentage and gives no derivation for his name.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ “and” prefixes the proper noun חוּל “Hul”.

evidence.note: Under וּבְנֵי אֲרָם, “the sons of Aram,” וְגֶתֶר names Gether between Hul and Mash.

analysis.evidence: The phrase וּבְנֵי אֲרָם introduces the sons of Aram. Gether is the third name, between Hul and Mash. The verse identifies the bearer but gives no etymology for his name.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ joins the personal name גֶתֶר to the preceding name in the list.

evidence.note: מַשׁ is the last of the four names listed under וּבְנֵי אֲרָם, “and the sons of Aram.”

article.summary: Genesis names Mash as a son of Aram. The meaning of his name is uncertain.

analysis.evidence: The phrase וּבְנֵי אֲרָם, “and the sons of Aram,” introduces the list. וָמַשׁ names its fourth member, after Gether. The verse gives no derivation for the name.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וָ־ joins the personal name מַשׁ to the preceding names.
